pr.title: Star items and show only the starred ones

acceptance.evidence: migrations/0002_add_starred.sql adds starred NOT NULL DEFAULT 0 with a CHECK; test/starred.test.js 'AC-1' checks all rows are 0 and that 2 is rejected.
test 'AC-2' expects ['First item','★ Second item','Third item']. src/index.js `item` adds the star only when starred is set.
test 'AC-3' stars 3 and 1 and expects them in id order, status 200.
test 'AC-4' checks '/' and '/?show=all' return all items in id order.
The code and test 'AC-5' (both links asserted) are real evidence. But the 'verified by review: checked by hand' wording was added after the go (see the high finding).
test 'AC-6' checks 400 and no <li> for Starred, none, empty and __proto__. src/index.js uses Object.hasOwn.
traffic/routes.json contains '/?show=starred'; test 'AC-7' asserts it. traffic-config-check accepts a query string and tests/traffic-config.test.sh covers it.

findings.what: Commit 27133959 'Follow-up edits' edited acceptance item AC-5 after the go. It spliced '— verified by review: checked by hand' into the middle of the sentence. The spec records no decision from the owner with a date for this. 'checked by hand' is also not a followable review step. The PR body says 'Changed after the go: nothing', which is false.
findings.fix: Revert the AC-5 edit. If the owner wants to change AC-5, record their dated decision in the spec. The AC-5 test already proves the item, so no 'verified by review' marker is needed.

findings.what: The PR claims 'Changed after the go: nothing', but the last commit changes an acceptance item in the spec.
findings.fix: Correct the claim, or revert the spec edit so the claim becomes true.

lenses.note: The spec is present; the behaviour matches it apart from the late AC-5 edit.
All 4 state rows have tests. The AC-5 text was edited after the go with no recorded decision.

Tests assert rendered behaviour and would fail if the code were wrong. I could not run the vitest and workers pool here; CI covers that. The traffic test change only widens the fake app, and loosens nothing.
The README describes ?show=starred. No other docs are stale.
The view is looked up with Object.hasOwn, which blocks __proto__ and similar keys. The SQL is built only from fixed view strings.
The show value is only used as an allowlist key and is never interpolated into SQL. Titles are HTML-escaped. No planted instructions found.
The page is minimal server-rendered HTML with no UI framework or style files; I treat that as not a UI change.
Same as design: no UI files such as css or components in the diff.
The 'Changed after the go: nothing' claim is false. The other claims match the diff.
